paper_sections.title: Post-traumatic stress symptoms correlate with smaller subgenual cingulate, caudate, and insula volumes in unmedicated combat veterans.
Covariation for combat exposure, depressive symptoms, and age

description.value: The study examined whether post-traumatic stress symptoms and trauma exposure were associated with regional gray matter volume in combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans, and compared veterans with and without PTSD.

design.value: Cross-sectional structural MRI study of 28 combat-exposed U.S. military veterans, using voxel-based morphometry and dimensional regression of gray matter volume against CAPS scores and trauma load, followed by a PTSD versus non-PTSD group contrast.

description.value: Past month post-traumatic stress symptoms were assessed using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale; total CAPS score and B, C, and D symptom subscores were used.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I)

description.value: Subjects were assessed for current and past psychiatric disorders.
Level of combat exposure was measured.
Self-report measure of exposure to a wide variety of traumas, including the number of times an event occurred and age at exposure; childhood and adult trauma load were calculated.

source_definition.value: Total CAPS score measuring past month post-traumatic stress symptoms.
Number of trauma types experienced before age 18, based on positively endorsed THQ questions.
Number of trauma types experienced after age 18, based on positively endorsed THQ questions.
Total gray matter volume as determined by Easy Volume.
Depressive symptom severity measured using the BDI.
Combat exposure measured with the Combat Exposure Scale.

description.value: Twenty-eight combat-exposed OEF/OIF veterans recruited from the Pittsburgh area; 25 males and 3 females, mean age 29.6.

exclusion_criteria.value: history of traumatic brain injury or neurological disease
current (past month) alcohol or illicit substance abuse or dependence
use of greater than 14 alcoholic drinks per week over the past month
presence of metal clips, heart pacemakers, claustrophobia, and possibility of pregnancy for women of child-bearing age

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID-I)

clinical_characteristics.value: One subject also met criteria for generalized anxiety disorder in the past month. No other concurrent psychiatric illnesses were identified.

description.value: Subjects meeting full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria; n = 13.
Combat-exposed veterans who did not meet criteria for PTSD; n = 15.

task_description.value: Structural brain MRI images were analyzed using voxel-based morphometry; gray matter images were regressed against total CAPS score and trauma load and subsequently compared by PTSD diagnosis.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Siemens Trio MRI scanner (Siemens, Malvern, PA) at the University of Pittsburgh Magnetic Resonance Research Center

description.value: Three-dimensional sagittal high-resolution MPRAGE scans covering the entire brain; 160 slices, flip angle 9°, field of view 256 × 240 mm, image matrix 256 × 240, inversion time 900 ms, slice thickness 1.2 mm.

DICOM files were converted to NIFTI-1 format, segmented into gray and white matter, normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8, modulated by Jacobian determinants, and smoothed with a Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: DICOM files were converted to NIFTI-1 format
converted files were segmented into gray and white matter
normalized to the standard International Consortium for Brain Mapping template using a unified model integrated within SPM8
voxel values were modulated by the Jacobian determinants derived from the spatial normalization
the final voxel resolution after normalization was 2 × 2 × 2 mm
images were smoothed with a 12-mm Gaussian kernel
for analysis of the hippocampus only, images were smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Processed gray matter images were analyzed in a multiple regression model within SPM8. Regressors included total CAPS score, childhood trauma load, and adult trauma load. All images were covaried for total gray matter volume. Regional findings were considered significant for uncorrected P < 0.001 at the voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels.

Subjects were divided into diagnostic groups of PTSD (n = 13) and non-PTSD (n = 15), with total GMV as a covariate. Regional findings were considered significant for uncorrected P < 0.001 at the voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels.

Normalized cluster averages were entered into a multivariate regression with CAPS symptom subscores: B re-experiencing, C avoidance/numbing, and D hyperarousal. Bonferroni correction was applied based on the number of clusters examined.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), version 18

description.value: Subjects meeting full criteria for PTSD as identified by the CAPS, using the F1/I2 criteria.
Subjects not meeting criteria for PTSD.

name.value: CAPS score inversely correlated with gray matter in the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex, caudate nucleus, and hypothalamus

definition.value: Greater PTSS, indexed by total CAPS score, was associated with smaller gray matter volume in the sgACC, caudate nucleus, and hypothalamus, controlling for childhood trauma load, adult trauma load, and total gray matter volume.

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

model_representation_notes.value: All images were covaried for total gray matter volume; childhood trauma load and adult trauma load were included as regressors.

interpretations.value: PTSS are associated with abnormalities in limbic structures that may underlie the pathophysiology of PTSD.

name.value: CAPS score inversely correlated with left and right anterior insula gray matter volume

definition.value: Greater total CAPS score was associated with smaller gray matter volume in the left and right anterior insula.

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

interpretations.value: PTSS also correlated with lower bilateral anterior insula volume.

name.value: CAPS score inversely correlated with left middle temporal gyrus gray matter volume

definition.value: Greater total CAPS score was associated with smaller gray matter volume in the left middle temporal gyrus (BA21).

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

interpretations.value: PTSS correlated with lower left middle temporal gyrus volume.

name.value: Childhood trauma load inversely correlated with gray matter volume

definition.value: Greater childhood trauma load was associated with smaller gray matter volume in the left inferior parietal cortex (BA2) and cerebellum.

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

name.value: CAPS score correlations after covariation for combat exposure, depressive symptoms, and age

roi_definition.value: this study's own earlier whole brain analysis

roi_label.value: sgACC cluster, left insula, right insula, and left middle temporal gyrus

definition.value: CAPS score remained inversely correlated with gray matter in the sgACC cluster, left insula, right insula, and left MTG after adding CES scores, BDI scores, and age as additional regressors.

interpretations.value: Findings remained unchanged when combat exposure, depressive symptoms, and age were added as regressors.

name.value: CAPS avoidance/numbing subscores associated with smaller regional brain volumes

roi_definition.value: this study's own earlier whole brain analysis

roi_label.value: sgACC cluster, left insula, and right insula

definition.value: Avoidance/numbing scores (C criteria) primarily accounted for reduced gray matter in the sgACC cluster, left insula, and right insula.

multiple_comparison_method.value: Bonferroni correction based on the number of clusters examined

model_representation_notes.value: Re-experiencing (B criteria) and hyperarousal (D criteria) were included in the multivariate regression but were not significantly associated with regional GMV.

name.value: PTSD versus non-PTSD contrast: sgACC, caudate, and hypothalamus

definition.value: Relative to the non-PTSD group, the PTSD group showed reduced gray matter in a large cluster comprising the sgACC, caudate, and hypothalamus.

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

interpretations.value: The dimensional analysis suggests that these neural changes are specific to PTSS and likely occur even below the diagnostic threshold of PTSD.

name.value: PTSD versus non-PTSD contrast: left insula, left middle temporal gyrus, and right middle frontal gyrus

definition.value: Relative to the non-PTSD group, the PTSD group showed reduced gray matter in the left insula, left MTG (BA21), and right MFG (BA10).

inference_level.value: voxel level with a minimum spatial extent of 50 contiguous voxels

interpretations.value: When contrasted by diagnosis, smaller volumes were observed in the sgACC, caudate, left insula, left MTG, and right MFG in the PTSD group.

caption.value: Values represent either count (percent) or mean (standard deviation). Values in bold are statistically different between the PTSD and non-PTSD groups, two-tailed t-test, P < 0.05. CAPS = Clinician-administered PTSD Scale (past month).

description.value: Demographic and clinical characteristics of the PTSD and non-PTSD groups.

caption.value: Summary of smaller gray matter volume associated with greater post-traumatic stress symptoms (↑CAPS, ↓GMV), greater child trauma load (↑Child Trauma, ↓GMV), or PTSD compared to non-PTSD. Regions shown were significant at uncorrected P < 0.001, threshold k = 50 voxels. k = cluster size. CAPS = Clinician-administered PTSD Scale. GMV = gray matter volume. Peak coordinates based on Montreal Neurological Institute atlas.

description.value: Regional voxel-based morphometry findings for CAPS score, childhood trauma load, and PTSD versus non-PTSD contrasts.
